subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should maintainers approve the full `workspaceAccess: "none"` repair now, making only the isolated sandbox `/workspace` writable while preserving real-workspace isolation and read-only protected mounts across all sandbox backends?
rationale: The desired product contract is now clearer from maintainer discussion, but the implementation changes a sandbox write boundary and should not be queued without explicit security-owner acceptance of the complete backend/tool/docs proof shape.

options.title: Approve Isolated-Writable None
options.body: Implement the full cross-backend fix that makes sandbox-owned `/workspace` writable for `none` while preserving host workspace isolation and read-only protected roots.

options.title: Keep Current Fail-Closed Behavior
options.body: Leave `none` read-only and update docs/tool exposure accordingly, accepting that the isolated workspace cannot support I/O-heavy skills in that mode.

options.title: Split Security Design First
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers write a short sandbox write-policy note covering isolated workspaces, custom binds, skill roots, and remote backends.

recommendation.title: Approve Isolated-Writable None
recommendation.body: Implement the full cross-backend fix that makes sandbox-owned `/workspace` writable for `none` while preserving host workspace isolation and read-only protected roots.

likelyOwner.reason: This account merged the related read-only mount change and later closed the strict workaround while naming this issue as the canonical sandbox contract fix.
